title: Chicago violent crime: rates, clusters and regions
blurb: 2024 violent crime by community area: rates per 1,000, Moran's I and LISA clusters, then 6 contiguous SKATER regions.

steps.label: Rates by community area
steps.prompt: The attached files are Chicago's 2024 violent crimes with coordinates (crimes_2024_violent.csv: homicide, assault, battery, robbery and criminal sexual assault), the 77 community areas (community_areas.geojson) and ACS 2023 population by community area (acs_2023_community_areas.csv). Count the crimes in each community area by each incident's coordinates, compute the rate per 1,000 residents and map it as a choropleth. What is the citywide rate, and which community area has the highest rate?

steps.label: Are the rates clustered?
steps.prompt: Test whether those rates are spatially clustered with global Moran's I (queen contiguity, row-standardised weights), then map the local (LISA) clusters: high-high, low-low and the outliers.

steps.label: Six crime regions
steps.prompt: Group the 77 community areas into 6 contiguous regions with similar violent crime rates using SKATER. Map the regions and give each one's community areas, population and mean rate.

title: Schools within a mile of a site
blurb: Buffer a site in the Chicago Loop by 1 mile, select the schools inside it and find the nearest one.

steps.label: Count and nearest
steps.prompt: The attached schools.geojson has school locations. How many schools are within 1 mile of the site at 41.8827 N, 87.6233 W? Which one is nearest, and how far is it in metres?

steps.label: Show it on the map
steps.prompt: Show the site, its 1-mile buffer and the schools inside it on the map.

title: Incidents per 1,000 residents by zone
blurb: Point-in-polygon counts turned into rates: the zone with the most incidents is not the one with the highest rate.

steps.label: Rates by zone
steps.prompt: zones.geojson holds 9 zones with a population field, and incidents.csv holds incident locations (lat/lon). Count the incidents in each zone and compute the rate per 1,000 residents. Which zone has the highest rate, and what is it?

steps.label: Map the rates
steps.prompt: Map the rate per 1,000 residents for each zone as a choropleth.

title: Fastest route on a road network
blurb: Travel time from length and speed on every edge: the shortest route is not the fastest one.

steps.label: Fastest travel time
steps.prompt: roads.geojson is a road network: each line is an edge between two intersections, with a speed_kph attribute. Travel time on an edge is its length divided by its speed. What is the fastest travel time in minutes from the intersection at 41.87408° N, 87.65075° W to the one at 41.89222° N, 87.62683° W? How many intersections, counting the start, can be reached within 2 minutes of it?

steps.label: Show the route
steps.prompt: Show the fastest route on the map.

title: Where to put two facilities
blurb: A 2-median location-allocation: pick the 2 of 8 sites that minimise population-weighted distance.

steps.label: Choose the sites
steps.prompt: demand.csv has 40 demand points with populations, and candidates.csv has 8 candidate facility sites. Choose the 2 sites that minimise the total population-weighted straight-line distance from each demand point to its nearest chosen site. Which two sites, and what is that total in person-kilometres?

steps.label: Map the service areas
steps.prompt: Map the demand points coloured by the chosen site that serves each one, and mark the two chosen sites.

title: Land under a 5 m flood
blurb: A bathtub inundation model on an elevation raster, with NoData kept out of the flooded area.

steps.label: Flooded area
steps.prompt: coast_dem.tif is an elevation model in metres, with the sea along its southern edge. If water rises to 5 m, how many hectares are at or below that level? Treat it as a simple bathtub: every cell at or below 5 m counts.

steps.label: Show the flood
steps.prompt: Show the flooded cells on the map.

title: Vegetation change from two scenes
blurb: NDVI from red and near-infrared on two dates, and the area that lost vegetation.

steps.label: NDVI and loss
steps.prompt: scene_2020.tif and scene_2024.tif cover the same area on two dates; band 1 is red and band 2 is near-infrared. Compute NDVI for each date. What is the mean NDVI on each date, and how many hectares lost more than 0.2 NDVI between them?

steps.label: Map the loss
steps.prompt: Map where NDVI fell by more than 0.2 between the two dates.

title: Site suitability from three layers
blurb: A weighted overlay of slope and road distance, with water and wetland excluded.

steps.label: Score the cells
steps.prompt: slope_deg.tif, road_distance_m.tif and landcover.tif are aligned 10 m rasters. A cell is suitable if its slope is under 8 degrees, its road distance is at most 500 m, and its land cover is not 1 (water) or 2 (wetland). Score each suitable cell as 0.5*(1 - slope/8) + 0.5*(1 - distance/500). What is the total suitable area in hectares, and what are the centre coordinates of the highest-scoring cell?

steps.label: Map the score
steps.prompt: Map the suitability score.

title: Aftershocks of the 2019 Ridgecrest earthquake
blurb: A space-time filter on a USGS catalogue: events within 7 days and 25 km of the mainshock.

steps.label: Count the aftershocks
steps.prompt: usgs_comcat_ridgecrest_2019-07.csv is a USGS earthquake catalog. What was the largest event's magnitude? How many events occurred within 7 days after it and within 25 km of its epicentre, and how many of those were magnitude 4 or greater?

steps.label: Map them
steps.prompt: Map the aftershocks within 25 km and 7 days, sized by magnitude, with the mainshock marked.

title: Measuring area and distance correctly
blurb: No upload: the agent fetches the county boundary itself, measures it on an equal-area projection, and gives a great-circle distance.

steps.label: Area and distance
steps.prompt: What is the area of Champaign County, Illinois, in square kilometres? And what is the great-circle distance in km between Trafalgar Square, London (51.5080 N, 0.1281 W) and Notre-Dame de Paris (48.8530 N, 2.3499 E)?
